channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Tencent Kicks Off $5 Billion Bond Sale to Finance AI Spending
item.description: Tencent Holdings Ltd. began marketing dollar and offshore yuan bonds in an offering that could raise around $5 billion to support its escalating investments in artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Janice Huang

item.title: Muse Wonder Puts Meta's Aggressive AI Push in Focus
item.description: Meta Platforms released a new artificial intelligence model called Muse Wonder, which the company claims is a big leap over its predecessors. Riley Griffin has more on "The Asia Trade." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Earnings Season, AI & Oil Prices in Focus
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are RockCreek CEO & Founder Afsaneh Beschloss, Barclays Multi-Sector Aerospace & Defense Analyst Anthony Valentini, Former Fed Governor Betsy Duke, Robinhood Markets CIO Stephanie Guild, Inflation Insights Founder & President Omair Sharif, Gabelli Funds Portfolio Manager Macrae Skyes, & Neostellar Principal Willy Lee. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Neostellar’s Willy Lee on AI Landscape Ahead of Anthropic Pre-IPO Investor Day
item.description: Willy Lee, Principal at Neostellar, says attention on Anthropic’s potential IPO risks obscuring broader AI investment and adoption. He cited nearly $200 billion in U.S. venture capital deployed in the first half of the year—more than 74% of the prior year’s estimated total. He speaks with Scarlet Fu & Hema Parmar on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Barclays: “Generational Shift” in Aerospace & Defense
item.description: Anthony Valentini of Barclays says aerospace and defense is at an inflection point: newer, high-growth companies using commercial business models should be evaluated differently from traditional contractors and could achieve higher margins at scale. He describes the shift toward lower-cost autonomous systems as a generational change, with new entrants positioned to gain market share over the next decade. He speaks with Scarlet Fu & Hema Parmar on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Big Take: AI’s Giant Money Loop Has Echoes of 2008
item.description: A web of circular investments is powering the AI boom, but it’s also amplifying global imbalances and stirring echoes of the 2008 financial crisis. Bloomberg's Shawn Donnan joins David Gura on the Big Take podcast to explain. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Applied Materials Will Double Sales, Not Headcount, Thanks to AI
item.description: Applied Materials Inc. expects to double revenue over the next few years, without a commensurate rise in hiring, because it’s relying more on artificial intelligence tools for things like product development and quality control.
item.dc:creator: Dina Bass

item.title: Meta Releases New AI Model Called Muse Wonder
item.description: Meta Platforms, parent company of Facebook, has released a long-awaited artificial intelligence model called Muse Wonder. This model is said to be competitive with OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude. Meta stock rose on the news. Mandeep Singh of Bloomberg Intelligence has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Robinhood CIO on Investment Ideas Ahead of Earnings
item.description: Stephanie Guild, CIO at Robinhood Markets, said rising bond yields have not yet diminished equities’ appeal. She attributed the increase in yields largely to strong capital spending demand and growth, rather than inflation alone, noting that some areas—particularly consumers—have not seen comparable growth. She speaks with Scarlet Fu & Hema Parmar on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tesla Cybercab to Make European Debut at Paris Motor Show
item.description: Tesla's Cybercab will make its first appearance in Europe at the Paris Motor Show this week. Elon Musk is trying to expand the company's footprint outside of the US. Bloomberg's Detroit Bureau Chief David Welch reports on Musk's ambitions and challenges. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Rallies as New Muse Wonder Model Heats up AI Race | Closing Bell
item.description: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Scarlet Fu, Hema Parmar, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Staggering Costs of a Single Data Center, From Land to Chips
item.description:
Roughly $750 billion. That’s how much Meta Platforms Inc., Amazon.com Inc., Microsoft Corp. and Google owner Alphabet Inc. are expected to devote to capital expenditures this year alone.
That’s more than the entire gross domestic product of Ireland or Belgium. More than half of what all of the companies in the S&P 500 Index spent in total last year. Enough to cut a $5,500 check for every household in the US. Ian King, Bloomberg News US Semiconductor Reporter & Lynn Doan, Bloomberg News Managing Editor for Technology, join Businessweek Daily to break down the true cost of a single data center. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Apple Plans to Compete in the Home: Power On
item.description: Apple is finally ready to unveil its new smart home strategy, seeking to plug a major hole in its ecosystem. Also: New details on the company’s Mac and iPad event near the end of October, and the latest on Apple’s push to demo the iPhone Duo at retail stores. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman joins Ed Ludlow for his latest edition of Power On on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How the OpenAI, Anthropic IPOs Could Lift the Veil on AI Economics
item.description: VistaShares portfolio manager and DVX Ventures principal David Fetherstonhaugh says investors are increasingly looking for proof that massive AI spending is generating returns. He discusses why private companies like OpenAI and Anthropic leave a key part of the AI economy opaque and how their eventual IPOs could bring greater transparency to the ecosystem. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bumble in Talks to Be Taken Private for $1 Billion, WSJ Says
item.description: Shares of dating-app company Bumble Inc. soared after the Wall Street Journal reported that it’s in advanced talks to be taken private for around $1 billion.
item.dc:creator: Samantha Murphy Kelly

item.title: Cisco, Nvidia Tackle AI’s Growing Data Center Bottleneck
item.description: Cisco is partnering with Nvidia on a new generation of optical networking technology designed to handle the exploding amount of data moving through AI data centers. Cisco President and Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel explains why increasingly powerful AI agents could consume far more network bandwidth than humans performing the same tasks, and how faster, more power-efficient connections could help hundreds of thousands of GPUs operate together while lowering the cost of AI. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fidelity: Tech Stocks Can Keep ‘Climbing the Wall of Worry’
item.description: Fidelity’s Denise Chisholm says technology stocks have undergone an unusually large valuation reset even as earnings expectations continue to rise, potentially leaving the sector positioned for further gains. She discusses why tech’s roughly 30% multiple contraction may already reflect concerns about slowing AI and technology spending, and why historical data suggests a slowdown in tech capex doesn’t necessarily mean a contraction. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Says New Muse Model Hits AI Frontier After Aggressive Push
item.description: The Muse Wonder model will be a key test for Meta’s expensive and rebuilt superintelligence team.
item.dc:creator: Riley Griffin

item.title: Microsoft Playing Catch-Up in Build-Out of Data Centers
item.description: The software company slowed spending, but now finds itself falling behind
item.dc:creator: Matt Day and Brody Ford

item.title: Microsoft and Meta Are Running Commercials to Sell Data Centers to Locals
item.description: Data centers aren’t popular with local communities. Microsoft and Meta are running PR campaigns to fix that.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford
